items.title: [Bug]: The message API doesn't support min_tokens for now
items.author: nantianzhuye
items.summary: The vLLM message API lacks min_tokens support, causing graph/eager mode conflicts and node freezes in PD-separation deployments when EOS is prefetched prematurely.
items.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
vllm version：v0.30.0
weight：ds v4.1 1017
</details>


### 🐛 Describe the bug

currently, min_tokens can be used in the responses API.but it is not supported in the message API.

When we use the PD separation deployment method, the response interface doesn't support the min_tokens parameter. The P node might infer an EOS, causing the request to be prefetched by a DP on the D node. At this point, the graph mode can easily switch to eager mode, leading to different DPs running different graph modes, which can then cause the D node to freeze.

items.author: lucamotz
items.summary: Adds handshake-time validation to reject P/D pairs where KV cache groups have mismatched block-size scaling ratios, preventing silent KV corruption in Mamba hybrid models.

## Overview

NIXL pairs every KV cache group's blocks at one P/D block size ratio, which comes from the lcm of the groups' block sizes. If one group's own P/D ratio differs, that group's KV lands at the wrong tokens without an error. This PR adds the groups' block sizes to the handshake metadata and rejects such peers at the handshake.

## Claims

- A P/D pair whose KV cache groups' block sizes don't all change by the same ratio fails the handshake with `NotImplementedError`, in pull and push. Before, Mamba hybrids passed the handshake. The transfer then put that group's KV at the wrong tokens

Fix early block reuse when a `MultiConnector` has a child connector that loads KV but its top-level `kv_role` is `kv_producer`. ### What does this PR do?

When the SandboxFusion server is overloaded (e.g. EMFILE reported as `SandboxError`, or 502/503 from a gateway), test cases fail for infrastructure reasons and correct programs are silently scored 0.0. Today `call_sandbox_api` retries only HTTP 504.

- Also retry HTTP 500/502/503, connection errors (including connect timeouts) and `SandboxError` responses. Retry count and delay are unchanged.
- Mark cases the sandbox could not judge with `metadata["infra_error"] = True`, checked with `is_infra_error()`. HTTP 4xx is not marked, since it can be caused by the model

## Why?

- `--enable-return-routed-experts` keeps every token's routed expert ids in a device buffer and a pinned host cache, and returns them in the response, all as int32.
- The ids are small. They run from `-1` (padding) to `num_experts - 1`, and models have far fewer than 32,768 routed experts, so half of every int32 is wasted.
- The bytes add up:
  - The pinned host cache is 216 GiB for Kimi-K3 with DCP16.
  - One response with 32k tokens × 60 MoE layers × top-8 carries 62.9 MB of ids (84 MB after base64).

items.title: [Doc] Add Apple Silicon (Metal) weight compatibility note to the Apple install page
items.author: alex7092
items.summary: vLLM-Metal loads weights through MLX, which requires checkpoints. Some models, such as, only ship legacy weights and fail with. [Discussion: Documentation preview: https://vllm--65043.org.readthedocs.build/en/65043/]
items.body:
## Purpose

Warns Apple Silicon (vLLM-Metal) users that some models cannot be loaded:

1. vLLM-Metal loads weights through MLX, which requires `.safetensors` checkpoints.
2. Some models, such as `facebook/opt-125m`, only ship legacy `.bin` weights and
   fail with `FileNotFoundError: No safetensors found in ...`.
3. Use a model that ships safetensors instead, for example `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (the
   default model for `vllm serve`) or an MLX-optimized model from

items.title: [Fix] [AMD] aiter: Decode DCP over a non-fp8 KV cache on Gluon instead of the asm kernel
items.author: yuychang
items.summary: It is a8w8: it casts q to fp8 and passes the KV cache's fp8 scale. aiter raises, and the server fails during CUDA graph capture.
items.body:
## Motivation

- With `--dcp-size > 1`, the aiter DCP decode defaults to the asm kernel. It is a8w8: it casts q to fp8 and passes the KV cache's fp8 scale.
- A bf16 KV cache, the default, has no scale. aiter raises `fp8 Q requires q_scale and kv_scale`, and the server fails during CUDA graph capture.

## Modifications

- The asm DCP decode now also requires an fp8 KV cache. Other caches use the existing Gluon DCP decode, and fp8 caches are unchanged.
- The backend logs once when `asm` was requested but the cache rules it out. It fails clearly at startup if Gluon is unavailable for this route.

items.title: Fix math_dapo Minerva extraction for markdown-decorated answers
items.author: siddhant-rajhans
items.summary: The existing regex captures the markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0. Fixes #8449 ## Root cause The Minerva answer pattern matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line.
items.body:
## Bug

Models commonly wrap the Minerva `Answer:` label in markdown bold/italic (`**Answer:** 42`, `Answer: **42**`, `**Answer:**\n\n42`). The existing regex captures the `*` markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0.

Fixes #8449

## Root cause

The Minerva answer pattern `(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^\n]+)` matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line. When models decorate with markdown:

| Input | Extracted | After normalize | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| `**Answer:** 42` | `** 42` | `**42` | -1.0 |
| `Answer: **42**` | `**42**` | `**42**` |

## Overview

On ROCm, `aiter.mla.get_meta_param` is a `functools.lru_cache` (default 128 entries) that returns a device tensor, `num_kv_splits_indptr`. A CUDA graph captured around `mla_decode_fwd` keeps only that tensor's address, and the cache entry is its only owner. Once enough new batch shapes evict the entry, the memory is reused and every replay of that graph reads garbage split offsets: decode output silently turns to gibberish while prefill stays correct. items.author: vorapolsiloai
items.summary: Under concurrent image traffic that executor becomes the bottleneck: requests queue for preprocessing while the GPU waits. This sizes the multimodal preprocessing executor by the existing when the processor cache is off, so images are preprocessed in parallel.
items.body:
## Purpose

With the multimodal processor cache off (`--mm-processor-cache-gb 0`, common when every request carries a new image), each request's image preprocessing (decode, resize, normalize, patchify) runs on a single-worker executor in the API server. Under concurrent image traffic that executor becomes the bottleneck: requests queue for preprocessing while the GPU waits. This sizes the multimodal preprocessing executor by the existing `--renderer-num-workers` when the processor cache is off, so images are preprocessed in parallel. No new option; default 1 = current behaviour.

items.title: Enter the paged-stash capacity reduction on every rank
items.author: Connor-XY
items.summary: Fixes a deadlock in paged-stash MoE overflow detection where dense-only pipeline stages skip an all_reduce collective, causing NCCL timeout hangs.
items.body:
**Why.** `PagedStashRunner.check_moe_overflow` first votes over WORLD on whether any rank went over its receive budget. When one did, a second `all_reduce` takes the MAX of the receive capacity the step needed. Only ranks whose model chunks hold an MoE layer that reports a required capacity entered that second call: NCCL EP built in non-eager mode.
- A pipeline stage made only of dense layers has no such layer, so it skipped the reduction. The MoE stages waited in it while the dense stage moved on to the rerun.
- The result is a deadlock until the NCCL timeout, or a later WORLD collective pair

With `--attn-dp-size > 1`, DFlash keeps the draft eager on every device, and any DP round with an idle rank falls back to eager target verify on all ranks.

**Why.** `examples/run_simple_mcore_train_loop.py` trains nothing. It wraps the model in Megatron Core's `DistributedDataParallel`, then steps a `torch.optim.Adam` over the parameters.

- The loop never calls `zero_grad_buffer()`, so `main_grad` holds the sum of every iteration's gradients.
- The bug came in with the DDP wrap in feb68a3d9e.

## Problem and proposed behavior

The NIXL prefill bootstrap loop currently lets metadata decoding errors escape the receive loop. A malformed registration or transfer message can therefore terminate the bootstrap thread; transfer parsing can also fail after an empty room entry has already been created.

This is an initial draft for a narrow part of the control-loop fault isolation work tracked in #34510, following the earlier work in #35281.

## Included in this draft

- Parse GUARD registration/transfer metadata completely before registering a peer or publishing transfer metadata to a room.

## Description

The SWA per-layer path in KVCacheManagerV2 reuses persistent host staging tensors as sources for non-blocking device copies. - copy_idx is copied into a fresh host snapshot;

The token-to-request mapping kernel in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/metadata.py` runs a 256-lane binary search. items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: Fixes scheduler race where early batch result processing was decided after scheduling, causing completed requests to incorrectly ride into the next batch launch.
items.body:
Stacks on #43900.

items.author: vorapolsiloai
items.summary: This adds an opt-in, time-bounded hold: while decodes run, waiting requests stay in WAITING until the oldest has waited, so arrivals batch into one prefill wave. disables the hold when few requests are in the engine (a low-concurrency workload has nothing to b…
items.body:
## Purpose

While decodes are running, the v1 scheduler admits new prefills as they arrive, so a burst of concurrent requests is prefilled one or two at a time over many steps, and every step with a prefill slows all running decodes. This adds an opt-in, time-bounded hold: while decodes run, waiting requests stay in WAITING until the oldest has waited `VLLM_PREFILL_HOLD_MS`, so arrivals batch into one prefill wave. `VLLM_PREFILL_HOLD_MIN_REQS` disables the hold when few requests are in the engine (a low-concurrency workload has nothing to batch). Default 0 = off, no behaviour change.

items.author: YuvrajSinghBhadoria2
items.summary: This PR addresses issue #63943 by fixing the Triton MoE naive block assignment to only be used for batch size 1. [Discussion: @liulanze @bnellnm @mgoin This PR fixes issue #63943 (Triton MoE naive block assignment causing 8-52]
items.body:
## Summary

This PR addresses issue #63943 by fixing the Triton MoE naive block assignment to only be used for batch size 1.

## Problem

The naive block assignment path in `_prepare_expert_assignment()` is taken when:
```python
num_tokens * top_k_num * 4 <= global_num_experts
```

On this path, every (token, expert) pair gets its own block, so an expert chosen by several tokens in the batch has its weights read once per pair. On bandwidth-limited GPUs (NVIDIA GB10 / DGX Spark with LPDDR5x), this causes 8% to 2x slower decode for device-resident weights.

## Solution

Only use the naive block
discussion: @liulanze @bnellnm @mgoin This PR fixes issue #63943 (Triton MoE naive block assignment causing 8-52% decode slowdown on bandwidth-limited GPUs). The fix is a minimal one-line change: only use naive assignment at batch=1 to avoid repeated r

items.title: Allow reset_prefix_cache to clear cached prefixes without preempting running requests
items.author: Asthenia0412
items.summary: The endpoint currently offers two behaviors while requests are running: - Default mode: the reset fails while any block is held by running requests. Under sustained load, the window where nothing is in flight can be vanishingly small or absent entirely.
items.body:
## Background

Issue #64853 requested a new behavior for `reset_prefix_cache` that clears
the prefix cache without preempting running requests. The endpoint currently
offers two behaviors while requests are running:

- **Default mode**: the reset fails (`success: false`) while any block is held
  by running requests. Under sustained load, the window where nothing is in
  flight can be vanishingly small or absent entirely.
- **`reset_running_requests=true`**: the reset succeeds, but every running
  request is preempted and restarts from scratch, adding repeated prefill
  work on top of the cach

items.author: AkiYangDev
items.summary: Sparse KV offload stores host KV by request ID and sequence position, while radix cache owns physical token slots. When a new request reuses a prefix, only its new tokens are offloaded to its host row.
items.body:
## Summary

Sparse KV offload stores host KV by request ID and sequence position, while radix cache owns physical token slots. When a new request reuses a prefix, only its new tokens are offloaded to its host row. Prefill reads the unwritten prefix from that row, and decode can copy the same wrong data into its device cache. Reusing the original request row can also overwrite a prefix still retained by radix cache.

items.title: Start a chunked prefill only when its whole prompt fits
items.author: lmcafee-nvidia
items.summary: With chunked prefill enabled, the dynamic engine can stop making progress under KV-cache pressure, and never returns. lets a new request start a chunked prefill when the KV cache has room for one prompt token.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

With chunked prefill enabled, the dynamic engine can stop making progress
under KV-cache pressure, and `generate()` never returns.
`_can_schedule_chunked_prefill()` lets a new request start a chunked
prefill when the KV cache has room for one prompt token. A long prompt can
therefore start, take the last free blocks, and then wait for one more
block. A partial chunked prefill keeps its blocks until it finishes and is
never preempted. Requests decoding beside it then pause for want of a
block. If they hold no more blocks than the paused-block budget, nothing is
evicted

items.title: Megatron-FSDP: end the pipelined HFSDP prefetch window on an FSDP unit boundary.
items.author: rapatel
items.summary: With, a DP-Outer bucket larger than the remaining prefetch size could end the DP-Inner prefetch window partway through the next FSDP unit. The rest of that unit was then gathered only at its own pre-forward hook, on the critical path.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
With `hfsdp_param_gather_overlap`, a DP-Outer bucket larger than the remaining prefetch size could end the DP-Inner prefetch window partway through the next FSDP unit. The rest of that unit was then gathered only at its own pre-forward hook, on the critical path. The window now finishes the FSDP unit it ends inside, which exceeds the size by at most one unit and never walks further.

## Description

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4/FP8 checkpoints store the PLE n-gram table as FP8 e4m3 plus a scalar

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Starts all distillation teachers at once instead of one after another, which is what dominates startup when the recipe has many teachers.

`MultiTeacherModelManager` used to build one `TeacherModelManager` per teacher in a plain `for` loop, and each constructor blocked until that teacher's vLLM servers were fully up. With N teachers the wall clock was N x (engine init + CUDA graph capture). Teachers run on disjoint devices and share nothing, so this serialization was pure latency.

items.title: [None][fix] Reject variable-width beam search under overlap
items.author: jongukc
items.summary: With the overlap scheduler, two concurrent requests whose widens (for example ) can read KV that no forward wrote. To keep the batch width uniform, the scheduler skips one request for an iteration while its generation position still advances.
items.body:
Under the overlap scheduler, concurrent requests that widen through beam_width_array can be skipped for one iteration to keep the batch width uniform while their generation position still advances. Their next attention step then reads a KV position that no forward wrote. Reject a changing beam_width_array at request validation when overlap is enabled; constant arrays and disable_overlap_scheduler=True are unaffected. Document the restriction.

items.title: fix(ppo): reduce cancellation in k3 KL estimates
items.author: LingYi-Liang
items.summary: This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close. With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 wh…
items.body:
## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 where an 80-digit reference gives 4.9986626e-11. The helper feeds the reported KL term and configured KL loss/reward paths; the Search-R1 example selects `low_var_kl` with a nonzero KL-loss coefficient.

## Description

In `KimiK3MoERuntime` the shared expert runs on an auxiliary stream alongside the routed MoE and today starts right after the router. items.author: 0z5a

items.body:
## Problem

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

How it happens:

- slime's colocated sender calls `update_weights_from_tensor` with `serialized_named_tensors`, `load_format="flattened_bucket"` and `weight_version`. It sets neither `selector` nor `disable_draft_model`.
- SGLang then fans the update out to every runner, because its default is `selector="all"`. The DFLASH worker

items.author: catherinelee274
items.summary: Fixes the Triton fused linear cross-entropy (, used with ) so a confident label keeps its logprob and gradient. Before this change the forward formed, where sums over every logit, including the label's own 1.0.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes the Triton fused linear cross-entropy (`verl/utils/kernel/kernels.py`, used with `use_fused_kernels=True`) so a confident label keeps its logprob and gradient. items.author: ZiyiXu06
items.summary: Fix the generic torch fused forward path for FSDP2-managed LM heads, including models such as Qwen3. Previously, the fused forward accessed directly, bypassing the LM head's FSDP2 hooks and potentially mixing regular Tensors with DTensors during matrix multipl…
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fix the generic torch fused forward path for FSDP2-managed LM heads,
including models such as Qwen3.

Previously, the fused forward accessed `lm_head.weight` directly,
bypassing the LM head's FSDP2 hooks and potentially mixing regular
Tensors with DTensors during matrix multiplication.

This change installs a fused LM head forward during backend initialization
and runs fused computation through `self.lm_head(...)`. It preserves
torch/liger backend selection and handles DTensor weights, device placement,
and hidden-state dtype inside the module boundary.

### What does this PR do?

`ReplayBuffer._wait_for_next_poll()` sleeps a hard-coded `poll_interval=2.0` between TransferQueue metadata syncs (used
by both the sync `sample()` and the async `wait_for_sampleable()`). The trainer therefore notices the last finished
prompt up to 2 s late, and `timing_s/gen` is quantized to multiples of 2 s (main, vLLM: 2.21, 4.21, 4.21, 2.21 … s;
SGLang: 2.28 s every step). This PR replaces the sleep with a wait on a small completion counter that rollout workers
bump when a prompt reaches a terminal status. On 8x MI355X GSM8K GRPO it cuts `timing_s/gen` by 22–31%

…he actor and reference model

vLLM never samples some token ids (the out-of-tokenizer tail, plus the vision placeholders): it sets their logits to -inf before sampling. The actor and the reference model still compute probabilities over the full vocabulary, so the policy that is sampled from and the policy being trained differ. Nothing in training then keeps the actor's probability on those ids in check, and it can drift freely since they are never sampled and never penalized.

items.title: [Bug] Startup health polling can block on an unresponsive server
items.author: LinzeShi
items.summary: If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach. This affects VIME's managed vLLM startup wait. [Discussion: independent check on main: this no longer reproduces.]
items.body:
### Bug Description

`_wait_server_healthy()` calls `requests.get(.../health)` without a timeout. If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach `is_process_alive()`.

This affects VIME's managed vLLM startup wait. The expected behavior is to bound each probe, then check process liveness and retry while the process is alive. The overall startup wait should remain unbounded for slow model loading.

### Steps to Reproduce

## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

## Background

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

The Megatron policy and reference log-probability paths materialize

- Support Megatron policy/reference computation with TP, SP, CP, and
  non-interleaved PP.

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

## Fix

Thanks to @kkyyxhll for catching in #2319 that SGLang ignores `sampling_params.temperature` when it computes input/prefill log-probs. items.body:
## Problem

`--rollout-temperature 0` is greedy decoding. That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.

`--eval-temperature 0` is unchanged; greedy eval remains valid.

## Change

`slime_validate_args` raises if `rollout_temperature <= 0`.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_megatron_argument_validation.py` — `0.0` and `-0.1` raise; existing validate-args cases still pass at the default `1.0`

used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

items.title: [Bugfix][Training] Avoid entropy grad graph when entropy_coef is zero
items.author: Henry-Jessie
items.summary: This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss. Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary.
items.body:
## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary. When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. The current implementation always builds the entropy autograd graph and clones the full logits tensor before entropy computation, which increases peak memory without changing the loss.
